name: NA-Selank Amidate

b.x: NA-Selank Amidate (N-Acetyl Selank Amidate) is a stabilized derivative of Selank with anxiolytic properties that community users compare to benzodiazepines, minus the sedation, tolerance, or dependence. Hundreds of reports across r/nootropics and r/peptides describe that profile consistently. NA-Selank Amidate is built on Selank, itself a synthetic heptapeptide analog of the endogenous immunomodulatory peptide tuftsin (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg). The N-terminal acetylation protects against aminopeptidases. The C-terminal amidation blocks carboxypeptidase degradation. Together, these modifications extend functional duration from minutes to hours after intranasal delivery. The parent compound Selank has real clinical backing. Zozulia and colleagues tested it against medazepam in 62 patients with generalized anxiety disorder over 28 days [1]. Selank matched the benzodiazepine for anxiolytic effect while adding antiasthenic and mild nootropic properties the drug comparator lacked. Separate preclinical work confirmed BDNF upregulation in the hippocampus after intranasal dosing [2] and measurable cytokine modulation under stress conditions [3]. Community protocols have adapted to the amidate form's longer half-life. Most users dose once daily at 300 to 400 mcg intranasally for 14-day courses, then take a 14 to 21 day washout. The most popular stack pairs it with NA-Semax Amidate, morning Selank for anxiolytic baseline plus morning Semax for dopaminergic focus. Formal clinical research covers native Selank only. The amidate modification uses sound mechanistic logic, but no human pharmacokinetic study has confirmed the assumed half-life extension.

NA-Selank Amidate operates through four converging pathways, all documented for the parent compound Selank in preclinical and limited clinical research. The first pathway accounts for the anxiolytic effect. Selank is a subtype-selective positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors. It increases inhibitory neurotransmission without directly binding the benzodiazepine site. That distinction matters; it explains the absence of sedation, amnesia, and physical dependence that define classical benzodiazepine use. The second pathway involves endogenous opioid regulation. Selank inhibits enkephalin-degrading enzymes (enkephalinases) in blood plasma with an IC50 of approximately 15 micromolar [4]. Blocking enkephalin breakdown raises endogenous enkephalin levels, contributing to mood stabilization and mild analgesia. Third, intranasal Selank administration upregulates BDNF mRNA and protein expression in the hippocampus. Inozemtseva and colleagues confirmed this in vivo [2]. BDNF-driven synaptic plasticity underpins the memory consolidation and neuroprotective effects that emerge by the second week of daily dosing. Fourth, Selank-derived peptides modulate over 30 inflammation-related genes in immune tissue. Yasenyavskaya's group tracked reduced IL-6, IL-1-beta, and TNF-alpha alongside restored anti-inflammatory IL-4 under social stress conditions [3]. This dual neuro-immune mechanism is the basis for Selank's stress-protective properties. The N-acetyl and C-amide modifications on NA-Selank Amidate do not change these mechanisms. They slow enzymatic degradation, extending the window during which the peptide remains active after each dose.
NA-Selank Amidate benefits center on anxiolytic and nootropic effects, with immunomodulatory properties layered underneath.
Anxiolytic effect without sedation or dependence. The parent compound matched medazepam in a 62-patient GAD trial [1] while preserving full mental clarity.
BDNF upregulation in the hippocampus confirmed in vivo after intranasal dosing [2]. Users consistently report improved memory recall and learning speed emerging by week 2 of daily use.
Rapid onset sets it apart from most nootropics. Community reports converge on 15 to 30 minutes to first anxiolytic effect intranasally, with peak activity at 1 to 2 hours.
Pro-inflammatory cytokine reduction (IL-6, IL-1-beta, TNF-alpha) under stress conditions, with restored IL-4 levels [3]. This dual immune modulation supports long-term stress resilience.

Effects persist 5 to 7 days after a 14-day course ends. Community users consistently describe a residual anxiolytic and cognitive benefit window that outlasts the peptide's clearance, likely driven by BDNF-mediated neuroplasticity changes.
Enkephalinase inhibition raises endogenous enkephalin levels (IC50 ~15 micromolar) [4], contributing to mood stabilization through the body's own opioid system.

Key Study

Zozulia et al. 2008 (PMID 18454096): native Selank vs. medazepam in generalized anxiety disorder (n=62, 28-day trial); Selank showed comparable anxiolytic efficacy with additional antiasthenic effects. Not specific to NA-Selank Amidate.

Half-life extension (~4-6 hrs estimated) is mechanistically supported but unmeasured in humans. Most recent primary Selank research: PMID 32621722 (2021 cytokines/stress model); no new 2022-2026 primary studies found.

Community Community dosing consensus from peptide research communities

Most NA-Selank Amidate comes as a pre-mixed nasal spray, so reconstitution typically isn't needed. If you're working with lyophilized powder (10 mg vial), add 10 mL bacteriostatic water for a 1 mg/mL concentration. Each unit on a U100 insulin syringe then delivers 10 mcg. So 200 mcg is 20 units, 300 mcg is 30 units, 500 mcg is 50 units. The per-nostril versus total-dose labeling trap catches more beginners than any other issue. A standard 300 mcg/pump spray, one pump per nostril, delivers 600 mcg total. That's an aggressive dose on day one. Start with one pump total per session, not per nostril. Refrigerate the spray the moment you open it. "It stopped working" is the single most common troubleshooting complaint in the community; the cause is almost always room-temperature storage. Opened sprays degrade fast and should be used within 30 days. If you notice the anxiolytic effect weakening before day 14, don't increase the dose. End the course early and extend your washout to 3 weeks. The amidate form's longer receptor occupancy may speed up GABA-A desensitization compared to native Selank.
Cycling Protocol

Russian clinical protocols for Selank use 14-day treatment courses intranasally 3 times daily. Many practitioners extend this to 4-week cycles with 2-week washout periods. The anxiolytic effect has been reported to persist for approximately one week after the last dose. No tolerance or dependence has been observed with repeated cycles. Some users employ continuous low-dose use (200 mcg 1-2x daily) without cycling.
NA-Selank Amidate Cycle

NA-Selank Amidate's estimated ~4-6 hr half-life produces sustained GABA-A receptor occupancy vs. native Selank's ~2-3 min plasma half-life. Prolonged receptor occupancy is theorized to accelerate GABAergic desensitization. Russian clinical protocols for native Selank already use 14-day treatment courses: community consensus applies the same 14-day limit to the amidate form, treating the longer half-life as a reason to use shorter cycles, not longer. The database entry's 4-week cycle (onWeeks: 4) is calibrated for native Selank, not the amidate modification.

No direct human safety data exists for NA-Selank Amidate as a distinct compound. Every safety profile detail below comes from native Selank studies or community reports of the amidate form. That evidence gap matters, because the extended half-life could change the side effect profile in ways that haven't been formally measured. The most clinically relevant concern is serotonergic overlap. Selank modulates serotonin metabolism and GABA activity in animal models. Anyone on SSRIs, SNRIs, or other serotonergic medications faces a theoretical interaction with no clinical data to quantify the risk. Increased sedation and serotonin-adjacent symptoms are the signals to watch for. Talk to your prescriber before combining. Benzodiazepine potentiation is documented preclinically. Selank amplifies diazepam's effects in animal models. Combining the amidate form with any benzodiazepine (diazepam, alprazolam, lorazepam) risks excessive sedation and additive CNS depression. This is a hard contraindication at anything above minimum doses. Paradoxical anxiety affects a minority of users, typically at doses above 500 mcg or after prolonged use without cycling. This reflects GABA-A receptor desensitization rather than a serotonergic mechanism. Reduce to 200 mcg; discontinue if it persists at that dose. Transient blood pressure reduction is observed in animal studies, lasting 1 to 3 minutes post-dose. Clinically, this matters only if you're on antihypertensives or prone to orthostatic hypotension. Check blood pressure with your first few doses. Mild nasal irritation or brief burning at the application site is the most common complaint. Occasional fatigue or drowsiness occurs in sensitive users. Transient headache in the first 1 to 3 days is reported by some; community users find Alpha-GPC (300 mg) mitigates this. Native Selank clinical trials (up to 28 days of daily dosing) reported no dependence, withdrawal, amnesia, or sedation. No toxicity emerged in studies running one month of continuous administration. Contraindications: pregnancy or breastfeeding (no safety data), known hypersensitivity to Selank, tuftsin, or formulation components, severe hypotension, active nasal infections or recent nasal surgery, children under 18, and autoimmune conditions where immunomodulatory effects could alter immune balance. When to stop and contact a physician: paradoxical anxiety that persists at reduced doses, excessive sedation (especially if using other GABAergic substances), signs of serotonin-like effects (agitation, tremor, hyperthermia) if on antidepressants, or symptomatic hypotension.
Common Issues & Solutions

Spray "stopped working": most commonly storage failure: opened sprays must be refrigerated (2-8C) and used within 30 days; room-temperature storage causes significant potency loss and is the #1 reported cause of non-response.

Per-nostril vs. total dose confusion: always confirm spray label: "200 mcg per nostril" vs "200 mcg total per session" doubles actual dose. At 300 mcg/pump, one pump per nostril = 600 mcg total; start with one pump total per session.

Tolerance developing before day 14: end course at first sign of diminishing anxiolytic response and extend washout to 3 weeks; the amidate form's longer half-life may accelerate GABA-A desensitization vs. native Selank.
Paradoxical anxiety or agitation: reduce to 200 mcg; more common at doses above 500 mcg; reflects receptor desensitization rather than serotonergic effect; discontinue if it persists at low doses.
Mild headache within 2 hrs of dosing: often responds to choline supplementation (Alpha-GPC 300 mg); if persistent, reduce dose and ensure adequate hydration.

NA-Selank Amidate is classified as a research peptide in the United States and most Western markets. It holds no FDA approval, IND application, or regulatory pathway status in the US. The parent compound Selank received approval from the Russian Ministry of Health in 2009 as an anxiolytic for generalized anxiety disorder and neurasthenia. That approval covers the native Selank formulation, not the N-acetyl amidate modification specifically. NA-Selank Amidate is not scheduled under the Controlled Substances Act. It is legally sold in the US for research purposes. Products are typically labeled "for research use only, not for human consumption." WADA status: Selank family peptides are not currently listed on the WADA Prohibited List, though athletes should verify current status before use, as peptide classifications are updated periodically. faqs.q: Is NA-Selank Amidate actually worth the price premium over regular Selank?
faqs.a: The dual modification (N-acetyl + C-amide) extends the half-life from about 2-3 minutes to an estimated 4-6 hours, so you can dose once daily instead of three times. That said, no head-to-head human study exists comparing the two. You're paying for convenience, not proven superiority.

faqs.q: Can I take NA-Selank Amidate if I'm already on an SSRI?
faqs.a: No clinical interaction data exists. Selank modulates serotonin and GABA in animal studies, which overlaps with SSRI mechanisms. Start low, watch for increased sedation or serotonin-like effects, and talk to your prescriber before combining.

faqs.q: Why does "per nostril" vs "total dose" matter so much with nasal sprays?
faqs.a: Because it can double your actual dose without you realizing it. A standard 200 mcL pump at 0.15% concentration delivers about 300 mcg per spray. One pump per nostril = 600 mcg total, not 300. Always verify your spray volume and concentration before dosing.

faqs.q: Does NA-Selank Amidate build tolerance faster than regular Selank?
faqs.a: Community theory says yes: longer receptor occupancy from the extended half-life may speed up GABAergic desensitization. That's why some users recommend 14-day cycles for the amidate form instead of the typical 28 days used for native Selank.

faqs.q: Can I use NA-Selank Amidate only when I feel anxious, or do I need to take it daily?
faqs.a: You'll get acute anxiolytic effects from as-needed use through its GABA-A activity. But the lasting cognitive and neuroprotective benefits from BDNF and cytokine modulation only come from running a full 14-day course. As-needed use is basically treating symptoms without building the underlying resilience.

faqs.q: Does NA-Selank Amidate need to be reconstituted?
faqs.a: No. NA-Selank Amidate is used as a nasal spray and is not reconstituted with bacteriostatic water.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of NA-Selank Amidate?
faqs.a: The half-life of NA-Selank Amidate is ~2-3 min (plasma); functional effects persist 6-8 hours via downstream gene expression. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.
